newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil steady in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil steady in quiet trade.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady late afternoon on Friday after losing about 25 cents in early day trading following large falls to overnight crude values, traders said.
"The gas oil is steady right now after the morning losses because of overnight crude falls," a trader said.
July swaps were indicated at $21.90/$22.00 per barrel while August was at $22.55/$22.65, both down 25 cents from Thursday, brokers said.
July traded twice this morning at $21.90 with August done at $22.60 and $22.55, they said. The market was untraded this afternoon.
Traders said gas oil's modest 25-cent fall compared to the 71-cent cut in overnight August Brent crude's close at $18.21 a barrel on the IPE was due to expectations of physical support.
Buying interests are expected to surface at around the $21.50 per barrel mark, they said.
On Thursday, the lowest offer in the physical market was at $164 per tonne ($22.00 per barrel) compared to a trade on Wednesday at $163 per tonne.
Improved sentiment was also attributed to a big draw in Singapore's middle distillate stocks.
Figures showed stocks fell for the first time since end May, by 1.331 million barrels to 10.744 million in the week ended July 2.
Traders said the 10.744-million-barrel stock level is still high compared to the normal levels of between six million and eight million barrels which they said is dampening sentiment.
Players are weary of the re-emergence of fresh offers should expected buying interest from China for August delivery fail to materialise.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread is steady with July regrade last quoted at $1.80/$2.00 per barrel.
Fuel oil is down slightly with July swaps quoted at $98.50/$99.25 per tonne, compared to Thursday's $99.00/$99.50, brokers said.
